name: Marc Technocrats Limited
summary: Hold — unresolved financial reliability and tradability. Marc is a growing, subcontractor-heavy engineering consultancy, not a civil-EPC contractor. Strong same-entity revenue growth and historically attractive incremental capital returns deserve credit. FY26 balance-confirmation and audit-trail limitations, aged receivables and an unexplained ₹3.1529 crore asset-note difference prevent an investable conclusion. Original-object IPO money supports the modeled base case, so funding is Conditional, not presumed failed. At the verified but stale ₹154.95 close of 14 October 2026, the funded diagnostic base earns 8.6%, below the 15% hurdle. Ordinary returns and actionable entry prices remain unscored.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved financial reliability and tradability. Marc is a growing, subcontractor-heavy engineering consultancy, not a civil-EPC contractor. Strong same-entity revenue growth and historically attractive incremental capital returns deserve credit. FY26 balance-confirmation and audit-trail limitations, aged receivables and an unexplained ₹3.1529 crore asset-note difference prevent an investable conclusion. Original-object IPO money supports the modeled base case, so funding is Conditional, not presumed failed. At the verified but stale ₹154.95 close of 14 October 2026, the funded diagnostic base earns 8.6%, below the 15% hurdle. Ordinary returns and actionable entry prices remain unscored. This is a growth business with quality limitations, not an evidence-backed compounder, proven fraud case or demonstrated insolvency. The key positive is capital-efficient engineering-service execution with low debt. The key risk is whether recognized fees turn into collectible cash. A lower price alone cannot cure financial-reliability concerns. Independent balance confirmations, corrected asset schedules, protected edit logs, current order-to-cash data and verified tradeability could reopen the assessment.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Marc Technocrats Limited; NSE Emerge MARC; ISIN INE0TD401015; listed CIN L74210HR2007PLC125245. The company was incorporated on 2 August 2007, converted to public status on 12 November 2024 and listed on 24 December 2025. It is not V Marc India or related Marc Fintech. The financial scope is standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. Commercial JV/MOU contracts are not automatically consolidated subsidiaries or acquisitions.

Information cutoff: 20 October 2026. Documents were retrieved on 22 October but dated by the cutoff. The last actual matched NSE price is ₹154.95 on 14 October, not 19 October. Issued shares are 17,313,383; indicative market capitalization is ₹268.2709 crore. The investor horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, exactly 4.999315537 years on actual days/365.25. The nominal pretax equity hurdle is 15%; ₹500,000 is an illustrative liquidity reference, not an allocation. Brokerage, tax and execution slippage are excluded.

G1 is Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Conditional and G4 Hold. Confidence is High on identity, exact statutory wording and observed exchange rows; Medium on historical organic growth, incremental returns and original-object funding capacity; Low on current balance reliability, realizations and complete liquidity. An audited source with express confirmation limitations is not treated as unqualified evidence of asset collectibility.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS is 5.36, displayed 5.4, with 100% factor coverage. GQS is 6.60, displayed 6.6, also fully covered. IAS is NS with 45% coverage, known weighted contribution 2.14 and missing-factor mathematical bounds 2.69–7.64. These bounds are not confidence intervals, forecasts or rankable scores. Exact Decimal arithmetic, weights and contributions are embedded; IAS uses unrounded BQS.

The factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 4, BAL 6, EXEC 5 and EARN 6; R NS, D 4, P NS and L NS. No GOV≤3 cap is justified by substantiated misconduct, and no persistent CAP/CASH≤3 cap is triggered. The historical aggregate organic capital bridge supports CAP without requiring private project cohorts. No undisclosed haircut is applied after scoring.

Material G2/G4 holds exclude this record from all numerical rankings. Business and growth scores describe the evidence but cannot create an investable IAS when return, expectations and liquidity inputs are missing. The final override is Hold — unresolved, not a disguised bottom-of-ranking zero.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Marc earns fees for engineering consultancy, supervision and quality control, detailed project reports, project management, surveys, technical/financial audits and pre-bid advice. It generally oversees the contractor doing the civil work rather than assuming the contractor's entire EPC balance sheet. Contract terms vary across rates, time, deliverables and milestones. Certification and invoice approval determine collections; services recognized before billing create contract assets.

FY26 gross billing of ₹81.4898 crore includes ₹11.7616 crore GST, leaving net revenue of ₹69.7282 crore. Professional/PMC technical fees of ₹40.8485 crore were 58.58% of net revenue; employee costs ₹9.2772 crore were 13.30%; materials/consumables ₹2.1331 crore were 3.06%. No inventory is reported. Subconsultants and partners enable an asset-light delivery model, but their quality, availability and payment needs limit margins and cash flexibility. This is neither subscription software nor a construction-inventory business.

Government-tendered infrastructure dominates historical access. SQC contributed 82.23% of FY25 revenue and 68.11% in H1FY26. JV/MOU contracts generated ₹33.7175 crore, or 70.61% of FY25 sales. They are service-delivery arrangements, not evidence of acquisition-led growth. Underlying government payers, procurement rules and partners can create correlated risk despite a diversified list of nominal customers. Recent private-contractor assignments broaden demand but also introduce different credit risks.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Qualification credentials, references, technical personnel, equipment and repeat relationships help Marc win work. These are real barriers to a new entrant but not proof of durable pricing power. Tender awards combine technical qualification with financial competition. Engineers and subconsultants are mobile resources. The proposed 3D survey vehicle could improve eligibility; an uncommissioned machine cannot be counted as an existing moat.

The prospectus's historical FY25 standalone peer table shows Marc revenue/operating EBITDA margin of ₹47.753 crore/21.68%, Rudrabhishek Enterprises ₹97.0051 crore/22.04%, Dhruv Consultancy ₹101.9647 crore/13.95%, and Ceinsys Tech ₹399.73 crore/23.23%. These are issuer-compiled historical comparisons, not independently refreshed current peer multiples. Dhruv is a closer infrastructure-consultancy comparator; Rudrabhishek has broader urban/planning services; Ceinsys has a different geospatial/technology mix and scale. No mechanical peer-median premium is assigned.

Marc's reported growth and margins are favorable, but peer variation and CARE's description of fragmented, tender-linked competition argue against a dominant franchise. MOAT 5 recognizes useful access and execution knowledge without assuming network effects or exclusivity. Losing skilled personnel, equipment eligibility or satisfactory references can impair this business without losing a factory.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Net revenue rose from ₹18.4381 crore in FY21 to ₹69.7282 crore in FY26, a five-year CAGR of 30.48%. FY23–FY26 CAGR was 51.24%. FY24 revenue of ₹26.0383 crore grew 29.17%; FY25 restated revenue of ₹47.7530 crore grew 83.40%, adding ₹21.7147 crore. FY26 added ₹21.9752 crore versus restated FY25, or ₹21.8552 crore versus the statutory comparative of ₹47.8730 crore. The respective growth rates are 46.02% and 45.65%; neither basis is silently substituted.

The same entity and no identified acquired operations support predominantly organic growth. Price, volume, headcount productivity and contract mix are not separately quantified, so all growth is not labeled volume. JV/MOU delivery and a wider service mix contributed. FY25 new orders of ₹27.2445 crore were below execution of ₹43.9539 crore, so acceleration drew on previous backlog. H1FY26 intake of ₹52.5939 crore recovered above ₹30.1279 crore execution. H1 revenue ₹32.1988 crore and PAT ₹5.7585 crore are six-month observations, not annual actuals.

The latest verified aggregate orderbook is ₹255.4623 crore on 30 September 2025. Comparing it with FY26 sales gives about 3.66 times but mixes dates and does not predict one-year conversion. The 26 August 2026 PMC award is ₹12.00095 crore; 27 August pre-bid advice ₹1.5 crore; 3 September PMC ₹1.74 crore. All are 12-month, ex-GST values. These ₹15.24095 crore awards cannot simply be added to the stale backlog without deducting execution and changes. REV 8 credits substantial growth while retaining these limits.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible growth comes from qualified bids, extensions and technical delivery, not from equating India's infrastructure budget with Marc's market. The base model reaches a ₹151.56 crore annualized revenue run rate by October 2031. That requires continued staffing, subconsultant capacity, milestone collections, guarantee collateral and equipment investment. No current net-backlog rollforward or audited hiring-productivity bridge proves this scale; it is an analyst scenario.

Across FY23–FY25, normalized operating NOPAT rises ₹4.6121 crore after retaining recurring bank charges. Incremental capital is ₹9.1023 crore when current FDs remain employed and ₹7.2999 crore when they are excluded as nonoperating. Incremental returns are 50.7–63.2%. Pledged margin deposits remain in capital in both variants. This coherent three-year same-entity bridge supports CAP 6, but is not proof of perpetual marginal returns. FY26 confirmations, cash absorption, the ICD and asset-note uncertainty limit forward inference.

FY26 CFO/PAT of 21% demonstrates that profitable growth can consume cash. Original IPO objects provide ₹17.5 crore for WC and ₹10.2545 crore for capex, plus limited GCP. July's proposed reallocation does not turn proceeds into unrestricted cash. The base honors original objects, excludes nonIPO FDs from funding and takes no new debt. Linked credit/guarantee stress breaches its reserve and requires a separately labeled hypothetical rescue. GQS 6.6 means strong reported growth with realization and deployment qualifications, not compounder status.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters held 73.55% without declared pledges on 30 September 2026. This provides alignment but concentrates control. The ₹8.45928 crore OFS benefited selling holders; it was not company funding. Fresh equity raised ₹34.12728 crore before expenses. FY26 director pay was ₹0.774 crore, total KMP pay ₹0.894 crore, related rent ₹0.054 crore and independent sitting fees ₹0.028 crore. These are not prima facie excessive relative to reported profit. The ₹2.0262 crore ICD's counterparty, purpose and terms need clarification; identifying Marc Fintech as related does not prove the ICD was a diversion to it.

Promises versus delivery: the December 2025 prospectus planned ₹10.2545 crore equipment/computer capex. March 2026 note 35 reports no object deployment. The 22 July notice still reports zero and proposes redirecting all capex funds to WC without a fixed timetable. Reported revenue execution and subsequent awards are positive evidence, but the planned capability and deployment return are not demonstrated. Voting approval and later use were not verified, rather than assumed not to exist.

The statutory report's positive opening opinion coexists with an express scoped disclaimer over unconfirmed transactions/balances. The application-level edit trail operated with no tampering found, but database logging and preservation evidence were deficient. IFC was described as effective with reliance on another auditor; this does not cure the separate gaps. CARO has inconsistent loan boilerplate around a ₹2 crore loan and an unstipulated repayment schedule. These need explanation, not an invented fraud conclusion. No defaults, auditor resignation or reported fraud were found. Previous ROC/PF delays were regularized. Answered tax summons and contract litigation are monitored as unresolved matters, not convictions.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 revenue was ₹69.7282 crore, PBT ₹14.2054 crore and PAT ₹10.5635 crore. Removing ₹1.7970 crore other income gives standard operating EBIT ₹12.6707 crore and EBITDA ₹13.4487 crore, margin 19.29%. Those standard measures add back all finance costs. More conservative normalization adds back only loan interest and retains recurring bank fees, giving EBIT ₹12.4725 crore, EBITDA ₹13.2505 crore and normalized NOPAT ₹9.2920 crore. The finance note's components total ₹0.01 lakh above its printed total; that small discrepancy is disclosed, not silently repaired. Model margins include recurring bank fees. Investment interest, asset-sale gains and sundry writebacks do not establish recurring project profits.

CFO was ₹2.2176 crore; cash capex ₹0.6023 crore; reported CFO-minus-capex proxy ₹1.6153 crore. The CFO bridge is PBT 14.2054 + D&A 0.7789 − sale gain 0.0151 − interest income 1.4896 + loan interest 0.0641 − receivables 3.2657 + payables 4.5021 + other liabilities 1.3240 − combined asset increase 10.2326 = ₹5.8715 crore before tax, versus reported 5.8716 due to rounding. Tax paid 3.6540 leaves reported CFO. Capex is an investing cash outflow, not the explanation for weak CFO. The ₹10.2326 crore asset movement includes current assets ₹7.0512 crore plus noncurrent assets ₹3.1814 crore; no additional imaginary cash outflow is charged for the note mismatch. CF D&A exceeds P&L D&A by ₹9,000.

Receivables of ₹12.4263 crore represent 65.0 endpoint days; contract assets ₹4.4563 crore add 23.3 days. More than one-year-old debtors are ₹3.8589 crore, 31.05%; over-three-year debtors ₹2.3367 crore remain classified good. Other current assets include TDS/TCS ₹5.7037 crore, tax refund ₹0.4342 crore and accrued interest ₹1.3486 crore, none automatically free cash. Note 11's ₹3.8187 crore total versus ₹0.6658 crore visible components leaves ₹3.1529 crore unexplained. MSME status/interest and leave obligations are not quantified. Gratuity was first recognized at ₹0.411438 crore, including ₹0.3689819 crore prior expense against equity; actuarial current/noncurrent timing differs from short-provision presentation.

Restatement F41 explains FY25 PAT ₹7.5753 crore to ₹7.4768 crore and net worth ₹28.1545 crore to ₹27.8537 crore through gratuity, deferred tax and prior adjustments. A ₹0.12 crore revenue/other-income reclassification leaves total income unchanged. Pledged margin FDs of ₹2.4924 crore moved between noncurrent-asset and FD presentation. FY24 opening cash of ₹11.7406 crore equals cash ₹2.1329 crore plus current FDs ₹8.4563 crore plus margin FDs ₹1.1514 crore. FY25 CFO differs between restated ₹5.4226 crore and statutory ₹5.0216 crore; both definitions are retained. FY22 cashflow was not found in the retrieved pack, so no fabricated five-year CFO total is shown. FY23–FY25 cumulative CFO/PAT of 102.6% is favorable; FY24–FY26 is 55.6–57.8% depending the FY25 basis.

Gross debt is ₹0.4930 crore, including ₹0.2106 crore current maturities. Cash ₹4.0478 crore and FDs ₹42.0574 crore are not all free: IPO earmarks are ₹30.893188 crore and the residual ₹11.164212 crore is not proven unrestricted. Guarantees ₹12.8052 crore are contingent, not present debt. The ₹3.4482 crore land and ICD receive no extra modeled equity value. Fresh shares expanded count 26.90%, diluting prior ownership 21.20%; OFS does not dilute. Current-share FY26 EPS is ₹6.1013, not weighted ₹7.23, and grows only about 9.9% versus statutory FY25 on preIPO shares.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The stale ₹154.95 reference implies market capitalization ₹268.2709 crore and reported P/E 25.40 times using the current share count. The normalized operating NOPAT multiple is 28.87 times. Deducting only reported cash above a ₹2 crore operating reserve and adding gross debt gives EV ₹266.7161 crore, or 19.83 times standard operating EBITDA. These are diagnostics, not certification of available cash. Removing all IPO deposits while capitalizing their interest would double count benefits.

The model bridges 31 March 2026 to the 20 October entry, then every fiscal period through exactly 20 October 2031. Each interval prefunds NWC, capex, collateral and identified old claims before its modeled operating receipts. It pays the old gross tax provision ₹3.654 crore without using TDS/refund assets, repays debt ₹0.493 crore, pays current actuarial gratuity, retains a ₹0.1 crore MSME buffer and settles the remaining issue budget. Original WC, capex, GCP and expense earmarks fund only eligible categories. There is no new borrowing, rollover, optional warrant cash or dividend. Future tax applies only to forecast earnings. Residual gratuity is deducted at terminal; unused earmarks, nonIPO FDs, ICD and land receive no extra terminal value. Entry signed surplus is reported but not added a second time. Terminal cash retains the reserve.

Base: 15% growth, 18% EBITDA margin after bank fees, NWC 15% of sales, collateral 5% of incremental revenue, capex 2.5% of sales and 12 times terminal EBITDA. It is funded at the selected reserve and yields 8.58% conditional annual return, terminal ₹233.83 per share. Conditional 12/15/18% hurdle prices are ₹132.69/₹116.27/₹102.22, not an actionable buy range. Bull: 25% growth, 20% margin, 12% NWC and 16 times exit produces 26.77%. Bear: 3% growth, 12% margin, 28% NWC plus 30 collection days, 50% aged-AR loss and a 10% guarantee call breaches its first pre-entry cash floor by ₹5.1765 crore. Bear ordinary and nonrescue conditional returns/entry prices are therefore null, regardless of terminal arithmetic.

The base's minimum upfront cash is ₹2.1736 crore against a ₹2 crore reserve. A ₹3 crore reserve fails by ₹0.8264 crore before modeled receipts. That is a reserve/timing sensitivity, not observed insolvency. The separate bear rescue raises ₹5.3367 crore gross and ₹5.1766 crore net, with 3% fees and whole shares issued at a 30% reference-price discount. It adds 492,016 shares and dilutes original ownership 2.76%. Its counterfactual return is -17.09%; no such financing is known to exist. Pre-entry rescue also changes entry share count and is separately identified.

Funded reverse crossings require 18.80%/22.09%/25.32% growth for 12/15/18% returns at an 18% margin and 12 times exit. The 15% hurdle needs terminal annualized revenue ₹211.27 crore. All 27 two-way cells are embedded: growth/NWC, capex/multiple, and margin/collection delay. Additional reserve, gross-tax setoff, FD release, capex timing and joint credit/guarantee stresses retain full rows and null nonrescue returns after any failure. A normalized post-reinvestment owner-cash perpetuity is a second valuation lens, not a device to override G2.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not generic SME volatility. It is that unconfirmed invoices and unbilled milestones may recognize margin before cash is secure. Delayed certification or payer remittance leaves subconsultants and employees needing payment, ties up collateral and forces lower-margin bids. Deferring equipment could reduce access to higher-spec tenders, worsening both growth and collections. Impairments destroy equity; discounted capital raising dilutes owners even if the company survives.

Counterevidence matters: historical restated cash conversion was strong, gross debt is small, fresh IPO funds are substantial and CARO reports no defaults or fraud. These facts make an automatic distress label unjustified, but do not authenticate specific debtor balances or resolve the missing database logs. The model distinguishes a funded original-object base from a linked stress gap. A modeled shortage under a higher reserve is not a claim that an actual payment was missed.

The thesis-break variable is collectible cash behind recognized fees, especially ₹3.8589 crore aged debtors and ₹4.4563 crore contract assets. A verified collections bridge is more valuable than another headline order. Material unsupported assets or proven misrepresentation would be gate events. One slow period or a procedural summons is an alert to investigate, not automatic failure. Multiple compression can also impair value even while the business remains profitable.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold appreciation in the exact five-year horizon requires about 38% annual price growth; tenfold about 58.5%, absent dividends. Large old backlog and small market capitalization are not proof of either outcome. At an 18% EBITDA margin and 12 times exit, the model's funded conditional 5× solution needs 46.09% annual revenue growth from March 2026 and a terminal annualized revenue base near ₹572.55 crore. That requires repeated replenishment, staffing and cash investment, not just execution of the old ₹255.46 crore orderbook.

No adjacent funded 10× crossing was found in the tested −5% to 50% growth interval. This does not prove mathematical impossibility; it means no supported funded solution is available within those assumptions. Even the 25%-growth, 16-times-exit bull case gives about 3.27×, below 5×. Relying solely on multiple expansion would substitute speculation for operating evidence. Both 5× and 10× are speculative/unsupported on the current information; no precise success probability is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections: baseline FY26 AR ₹12.4263 crore, over-one-year balances ₹3.8589 crore and contract assets ₹4.4563 crore. At the next results, seek subsequent receipts and certifications. An aged share above 35% is an investigation alert; proven material nonrecoverability or false confirmation is more serious.
2. Audit scope/logs: require independent confirmation of remediation of the 29 May 2026 findings, database logging and preserved records. Management reassurance alone does not reopen G2.
3. Asset schedule: reconcile note 11's ₹3.1529 crore difference. A validated tabulation correction can remove one issue; unsupported asset existence would worsen it.
4. Cash conversion: FY26 CFO/PAT was 21%; FY23–FY25 was 102.6%. Look for rolling 12–24-month conversion toward 80% with aged balances cleared. Persistent below-50% conversion alongside aging warrants lower CASH and renewed funding analysis.
5. Orders/access: obtain opening backlog + awards − execution − cancellations = closing backlog. Intake/execution was 0.62 times FY25 versus 1.75 times H1FY26. Sustained sub-one intake or lost technical eligibility is an alert, not an automatic valuation verdict.
6. IPO use: verify the object-variation vote, eligible deployment and returns. Ineligible use is a governance event; the July proposal alone is not proof of misuse.
7. Funding: track guarantees ₹12.8052 crore, deposit encumbrance, maturities and calls. Available liquidity falling below a chosen operating reserve requires a funded response, not assumed loan renewal.
8. Per-share economics: baseline shares 17,313,383, no options/warrants/convertibles and 73.55% unpledged promoter holding. Monitor normalized EPS, ICD recovery and new issuance; separate count expansion from ownership dilution.
9. Tradability: refresh official status, series and complete 20/60-session execution evidence. Missing rows are unknown. One 1,200-share lot requires ₹37.188 lakh daily turnover at 5% participation at the reference price.
10. Legal/compliance: obtain updated contract-case and summons outcomes and quantify MSME/leave exposures. Distinguish adverse adjudication from procedural inquiry. These are research milestones, not reminders, scheduled monitoring or trade orders.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved financial reliability and tradability. BQS 5.4 and GQS 6.6 summarize independently assessed business economics; IAS is NS. This is not an evidence-backed compounder candidate because business quality, moat, cash, key-factor thresholds and clear-gate requirements are not met. It is also not a substantiated governance Avoid or demonstrated distress case. Published original-object funding supports a plausible base, while forward realizations remain conditional.

The stale ₹154.95 reference does not deliver a supported 15% base-case return in the transparent model. Hurdle prices are conditional diagnostics only; ordinary entry prices remain null. A cheaper quote cannot fix the audit and asset evidence. The next useful step is reconciled balances and edit logs, current orders and collections, approved fund use and verified whole-lot tradeability. With that evidence, R/P/L and ranking eligibility can be revisited without erasing historical growth. Sizing examples are not portfolio recommendations.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources include the 22 December 2025 prospectus and all restated annexures F1–F41; the FY26 annual report's opinion, CARO, Rule 11, IFC and financial notes; a second issuer-hosted copy; FY21/FY22 statutory packs; the 22 July object-variation corrigendum; April 2025 CARE withdrawal; September shareholding; three NSE order disclosures; and dated exchange bhavcopies, security master and holiday calendar. Exact URLs, dates, hashes and claim locators are retained. Post-cutoff prices are excluded.

Units are crore except labeled shares, rupees/share and exchange turnover. FY22 originals are in hundreds of rupees, FY21 in rupees and later statements in lakh. Revenue is net of GST. Normalized NOPAT excludes other income and retains bank charges at a 25.5% tax assumption. Pledged guarantee deposits remain employed capital. CFO less cash operating capex is a reported FCF proxy, not automatically FCFF. Missing market rows are never silently filled with zero. Original source-number strings preserve precision separately from calculation outputs.

Open questions are balance confirmations, note 11 composition, edit-log remediation, MSME/leave obligations, aged/unbilled collections, ICD counterparty and terms, current backlog/payer concentration, object-vote outcome and deployment, unrestricted deposits/guarantee maturities, exact trading mechanics and full capacity, updated litigation and missing FY22 cashflow. Most important model assumptions are collection timing, margin, legally eligible funding, reserve, capex and exit valuation. Source-safe reconstruction verifies calculations and artifact consistency, not fresh authenticity of omitted original documents.

funding_notes: No fresh borrowing, no revolver renewal, no optional warrants, no unverified release of nonIPO deposits. Existing gross debt repaid upfront from unrestricted cash; interest zero afterwards.
Original WC, capex, GCP and issue-expense buckets cannot subsidize ineligible uses. Proposed capex-to-WC variation is unapproved in evidence; tested separately, never baseline.

Full old income-tax provision paid gross without using TDS/refund asset, avoiding optimism; future tax applies only to forecast earnings. Current actuarial gratuity paid once, remaining noncurrent gratuity deducted at terminal.
No dividend, new acquisition, NCI or lease obligation identified. Operating land is not added to earnings EV; ICD and residual FDs receive zero extra equity value.
Upfront NWC/capex/collateral/old claims prefunded before interval cash earnings; operating reserve covers lumpy collections only imperfectly. Periods are annual, not daily bank forecasts.

Entry cash signed surplus is reported, not separately added again; terminal equity adds only terminal cash minus reserve and residual liabilities. Unused restricted IPO money valued at zero rather than assumed distributable.
AR loss reduces modeled collection cash once; capital writeoffs to unexplained NCA do not create a second imaginary cash outflow. BG calls stress contingent payments, not automatic gross debt.
Pre-entry counterfactual rescue events are separately dated and change entry share count. They are not actual financing, and their returns are not actionable.
